title: Happy Birthday
description: The tune everyone ends up playing at a party. Learn it a line at a time, then add the three chords underneath.

steps.title: Before you start
steps.description: You've sung this a hundred times, but it's sneakier on the keys than you'd think. It starts low, on the G just below middle C, and later jumps up a whole octave. We're in C major, so it's all white keys. Every line opens with the same pickup: two G's for "Hap-py".

steps.title: Line 1: "Happy birthday to you"
steps.description: Play G G A G C B. The two G's are "Hap-py", up to A for "birth-", back to G for "-day", up to C for "to", and down to B for "you".
steps.hint: Start on the G below middle C. Count three white keys down from middle C: B, A, G.

steps.title: Line 2: "Happy birthday to you"
steps.description: Same start as before, G G A G. This time reach a little higher, up to D, then settle on C. That C is home, so the line should sound finished.
steps.hint: If you land on B, you've played line 1 again. The D is the white key just above middle C.

steps.title: Line 3: "Happy birthday dear..."
steps.description: This is the big moment. After the two low G's, leap up a whole octave to the high G for "birth-". Then walk down E, C, B, A through "-day dear" and the name.
steps.hint: The high G is the one just above middle C. Count up from C: C, D, E, F, G.

steps.title: Line 4: "Happy birthday to you"
steps.description: Last line. It starts up on F this time, not G: F F E C D C. Step down to E, drop to C, nudge up to D and finish back on C.
steps.hint: F is four white keys up from middle C: C, D, E, F.

steps.title: The C major chord
steps.description: Now for the chords. C major is home. The song starts on it and finishes on it. Play C, E and G together.
steps.hint: Start on C and skip every other white key: C, E, G. Any octave works.

steps.title: The G major chord
steps.description: G major sits under "you" at the end of line 1. It sounds unsettled, like it wants to get back to C, and line 2 takes it there. Play G, B and D.
steps.hint: Same shape as C, just starting on G: G, B, D.

steps.title: The F major chord
steps.description: F major comes in on line 3, right as you sing the name. It's the IV chord in C, and it gives that line its warm, lifted feel. Play F, A and C.
steps.hint: Same shape again, starting on F: F, A, C.

steps.title: The whole song
steps.description: Now play it from start to finish: G G A G C B | G G A G D C | G G G E C B A | F F E C D C. Take it slowly and sing it in your head as you go.
steps.hint: Wrong notes don't reset anything, so if you slip, find the right key and keep going. The jump to high G in line 3 is where most people stumble.

steps.title: Naming the chords
steps.description: You used C, G and F in this lesson. How would a musician describe those three chords in C major?

steps.title: Putting it together
steps.description: That's Happy Birthday. The three chords you learned, I, IV and V, turn up in a huge number of songs, so they're worth knowing well. Next, try holding a chord in your left hand while your right hand plays the tune: mostly C, G at the end of line 1, and F under the name.
